For this augmentation, reasonable implementation choices—not established SASRec-specific results—are Xavier-initialized source/target projections, zero projection biases, gate w=0 and b=0 (gate=0.5), and a small nonzero alpha. Pool only valid recent items at positions ≤t, normalize pooling weights by their valid sum with an epsilon safeguard, and return zero for empty histories. Mask after projections/normalization because biases can revive padding; exclude padded targets from loss. `padding_idx=0` alone does not mask downstream operations ([Embedding](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Embedding)). Consider branch-local LayerNorm and divide the projected dot product by sqrt(projection_dim) when components have roughly unit variance; cosine normalization needs its own temperature instead. This scaling follows the variance argument in [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762). Tune modest branch dropout, projection weight decay, and gradient clipping using validation.

By the chain rule, zeroing both bilinear projections kills both gradients. Zeroing only the target projection permits its update immediately, while source and gate gradients initially vanish; random-source/zero-target initialization parallels [LoRA initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08447). A trainable alpha initialized at zero can learn if the remaining branch is nonzero, but branch parameters initially receive zero gradients. Combining zero alpha with zero branch output can stall everything. Sigmoid derivatives are g(1−g): large positive or negative gate logits suppress gate learning; near-zero gates also suppress projection gradients.

For an alpha=0 baseline control, bypass branch construction, computation, dropout, and branch regularization. If construction is necessary, isolate all constructor/initializer draws with `torch.random.fork_rng`, including the relevant CUDA device; it restores RNG states ([PyTorch](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/random.html)). Preserve baseline initialization order, sampling, optimizer settings, and updates; unchanged seeds alone cannot preserve the random-number stream.
